answer: An agent economy can make reputation non-transferable by tying each identity to a scarce, costly stake that is slashed when its owner breaks a verifiable protocol rule. A grove of agents may let newcomers earn trust through small jobs, while a meadow records signed outcomes and a haven offers recourse for disputes. Creating many identities then requires locking more capital in each one; the attacker risks losing that stake, not merely discarding a free account.
